!57 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Issue 4722: a matrix layout request is dropped when the matrix type comes from a template.\0A//\0A// Look at the Buffer Definitions comment block near the top of the DXIL output, not at the\0A// source. One pragma at the top of the file asks for a single layout for everything below it,\0A// and the two struct members under it are the same 4x4 float matrix in the same cbuffer. Only\0A// the member declared outside a template gets the layout that was asked for; the one that comes\0A// through the template gets the compiler default instead. Nothing is diagnosed and the compile\0A// succeeds, so this block is the only place the difference is visible.\0A//\0A// The DXIL body agrees with the block: the two mul() calls consume different components of the\0A// loaded cbuffer rows, which is what a layout difference means at runtime.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Compiler Explorer presentation for issue 4722.\0A//\0A// Both members are declared under the ONE pragma at the top of this file, and\0A// they differ in exactly one way: the first goes through a template, the second\0A// does not. Everything else -- element type, dimensions, member name, the\0A// cbuffer they live in -- is the same.\0A//\0A// This file exists only to make the difference readable in one pane. The\0A// measured evidence is repro.hlsl and its controls, which vary one thing at a\0A// time; see manual-case-identity.txt.\0A\0A#pragma pack_matrix(row_major)\0A\0Atemplate<typename T, int X, int Y>\0Astruct ThroughTemplate {\0A  matrix<T, X, Y> M;\0A};\0A\0Astruct Directly {\0A  matrix<float, 4, 4> M;\0A};\0A\0Acbuffer CB {\0A  ThroughTemplate<float, 4, 4> A;\0A  Directly                     B;\0A};\0A\0Afloat4 main(float4 v : V) : SV_Target {\0A  return mul(A.M, v) + mul(B.M, v);\0A}\0A"}

!57 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Issue 4722: a matrix layout request is dropped when the matrix type comes from a template.\0A//\0A// Look at the Buffer Definitions comment block near the top of the DXIL output, not at the\0A// source. One pragma at the top of the file asks for a single layout for everything below it,\0A// and the two struct members under it are the same 4x4 float matrix in the same cbuffer. Only\0A// the member declared outside a template gets the layout that was asked for; the one that comes\0A// through the template gets the compiler default instead. Nothing is diagnosed and the compile\0A// succeeds, so this block is the only place the difference is visible.\0A//\0A// The DXIL body agrees with the block: the two mul() calls consume different components of the\0A// loaded cbuffer rows, which is what a layout difference means at runtime.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Compiler Explorer presentation for issue 4722.\0A//\0A// Both members are declared under the ONE pragma at the top of this file, and\0A// they differ in exactly one way: the first goes through a template, the second\0A// does not. Everything else -- element type, dimensions, member name, the\0A// cbuffer they live in -- is the same.\0A//\0A// This file exists only to make the difference readable in one pane. The\0A// measured evidence is repro.hlsl and its controls, which vary one thing at a\0A// time; see manual-case-identity.txt.\0A\0A#pragma pack_matrix(row_major)\0A\0Atemplate<typename T, int X, int Y>\0Astruct ThroughTemplate {\0A  matrix<T, X, Y> M;\0A};\0A\0Astruct Directly {\0A  matrix<float, 4, 4> M;\0A};\0A\0Acbuffer CB {\0A  ThroughTemplate<float, 4, 4> A;\0A  Directly                     B;\0A};\0A\0Afloat4 main(float4 v : V) : SV_Target {\0A  return mul(A.M, v) + mul(B.M, v);\0A}\0A"}
!58 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl"}
